      "title": "Persist the parsed Google tokens, not the safeParse result",
      "body": "parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a wrapper shaped like { success: true, data: tokens }, unlike the removed googleCredentialSchema.parse call. Saving that wrapper directly as credential.key moves all token fields under data. After any successful refresh, even with credential sharing disabled, the next service instance cannot parse the saved key with googleCredentialSchema. Persist the successful result's data instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Import the Prisma client used by Salesforce refresh",
      "body": "The new prisma.credential.update call references prisma without importing or defining it in this module. This fails type checking and, if type checking is bypassed, throws before the Salesforce connection can be created. Import the shared Prisma client before using it."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Replace the computed schema keys with actual token fields",
      "body": "Calling toString() on these Zod schemas produces the literal property name '[object Object]'; it does not declare arbitrary response properties. Both computed keys collide, and Zod strips ordinary fields such as expires_in, expiry_date, and refresh_token as unknown keys. With sharing enabled, a normal token response therefore loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates a NaN expiry, while Office365 retains its old expired timestamp. Define and normalize the supported expiry fields explicitly and preserve the required token properties."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Make delegated refresh responses compatible with their callers",
      "body": "The delegated branch returns an unread Fetch Response, while several callers expect the SDK or Axios result returned by refreshFunction. Google Calendar, Zoho CRM, and Bigin read response.data; HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly. None of those callers decodes the delegated response body, so enabling syncing makes valid refresh replies fail or yield undefined tokens. Normalize the response contract and adapt these callers instead of returning incompatible result types behind any."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Preserve existing refresh tokens when no replacement is returned",
      "body": "The literal 'refresh_token' fallback also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits a successful token response without a replacement refresh_token and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. This fallback overwrites the usable stored refresh token with that literal string, causing the next native refresh to fail and requiring reconnection. Leave an omitted refresh token absent so the existing value can be retained."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Pass the credential owner's user ID to Bigin token sync",
      "body": "The third refreshOAuthTokens argument is a user ID and is sent to the parent application as calcomUserId, but this call supplies the credential table's primary key. These IDs are unrelated, so the parent either cannot find the user or returns tokens belonging to another user whose ID happens to match. It also incorrectly delegates team-owned credentials because their credential ID is non-null. Carry credential.userId separately from the ID used for database updates."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Send Zoom's canonical app slug to the sync endpoint",
      "body": "The Zoom app is stored and installed with appId/slug 'zoom', as shown in its OAuth callback, but this request sends appSlug='zoomvideo'. The webhook also identifies apps by their canonical database slug. A parent application keyed by the same slug used to sync the credential will therefore fail to find Zoom tokens when they expire. Send 'zoom' rather than the integration directory name."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint",
      "body": "This new refresh request always goes directly to Salesforce and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ignored for this integration. When the parent application owns or rotates the refresh token, the local refresh token can be absent or stale; this mandatory request then prevents connection creation even if a valid access token was synced. Use the delegated refresh path when enabled and initialize the connection with its returned tokens."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Handle minimal sync responses separately from native provider responses",
      "body": "refreshOAuthTokens documents that the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but the delegated Webex response still goes through webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A valid minimal sync response is therefore rejected at the first refresh. Lark's delegated path similarly still expects its native code/data envelope and refresh-token fields. Add sync-specific parsing and preserve existing credential metadata rather than requiring the parent to return the native refresh-token response."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Identify the connected account before replacing its credentials",
      "body": "A user can have multiple credentials for the same app, including multiple Google Calendar accounts, but the webhook identifies a connection only by userId and appSlug and overwrites findFirst's result. A sync intended for the second account can replace the first account's tokens while leaving calendar selections and booking references attached to that first credential ID. Accept a stable connection/account identifier, or reject ambiguous matches rather than silently choosing one."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 83,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make initial credential synchronization idempotent under concurrency",
      "body": "The existence lookup and credential creation are separate operations. Two overlapping deliveries for a previously unsynced connection can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Subsequent deliveries update only one row through findFirst, leaving the duplicate with stale tokens. Use an atomic or serialized operation keyed by the synced connection so concurrent webhook deliveries cannot create duplicates."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 78,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Clear credential invalidation when fresh credentials are synced",
      "body": "Google, Zoom, and Webex can mark a credential invalid after an unrecoverable grant error. If the user reconnects in the parent application, this webhook finds that existing row but updates only its key, leaving invalid=true despite the replacement tokens. The credential remains marked disconnected and unavailable to consumers that exclude invalid credentials. Reset the invalid flag when accepting validated replacement credentials."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Persist the parsed Google tokens, not the safeParse result
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a wrapper shaped like { success: true, data: tokens }, unlike the removed googleCredentialSchema.parse call. Saving that wrapper directly as credential.key moves all token fields under data. After any successful refresh, even with credential sharing disabled, the next service instance cannot parse the saved key with googleCredentialSchema. Persist the successful result's data instead.

findings.title: Import the Prisma client used by Salesforce refresh
findings.body: The new prisma.credential.update call references prisma without importing or defining it in this module. This fails type checking and, if type checking is bypassed, throws before the Salesforce connection can be created. Import the shared Prisma client before using it.

findings.title: Replace the computed schema keys with actual token fields
findings.body: Calling toString() on these Zod schemas produces the literal property name '[object Object]'; it does not declare arbitrary response properties. Both computed keys collide, and Zod strips ordinary fields such as expires_in, expiry_date, and refresh_token as unknown keys. With sharing enabled, a normal token response therefore loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates a NaN expiry, while Office365 retains its old expired timestamp. Define and normalize the supported expiry fields explicitly and preserve the required token properties.

findings.title: Make delegated refresh responses compatible with their callers
findings.body: The delegated branch returns an unread Fetch Response, while several callers expect the SDK or Axios result returned by refreshFunction. Google Calendar, Zoho CRM, and Bigin read response.data; HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly. None of those callers decodes the delegated response body, so enabling syncing makes valid refresh replies fail or yield undefined tokens. Normalize the response contract and adapt these callers instead of returning incompatible result types behind any.

findings.title: Preserve existing refresh tokens when no replacement is returned
findings.body: The literal 'refresh_token' fallback also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits a successful token response without a replacement refresh_token and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. This fallback overwrites the usable stored refresh token with that literal string, causing the next native refresh to fail and requiring reconnection. Leave an omitted refresh token absent so the existing value can be retained.

findings.title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to Bigin token sync
findings.body: The third refreshOAuthTokens argument is a user ID and is sent to the parent application as calcomUserId, but this call supplies the credential table's primary key. These IDs are unrelated, so the parent either cannot find the user or returns tokens belonging to another user whose ID happens to match. It also incorrectly delegates team-owned credentials because their credential ID is non-null. Carry credential.userId separately from the ID used for database updates.

findings.title: Send Zoom's canonical app slug to the sync endpoint
findings.body: The Zoom app is stored and installed with appId/slug 'zoom', as shown in its OAuth callback, but this request sends appSlug='zoomvideo'. The webhook also identifies apps by their canonical database slug. A parent application keyed by the same slug used to sync the credential will therefore fail to find Zoom tokens when they expire. Send 'zoom' rather than the integration directory name.

findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: This new refresh request always goes directly to Salesforce and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ignored for this integration. When the parent application owns or rotates the refresh token, the local refresh token can be absent or stale; this mandatory request then prevents connection creation even if a valid access token was synced. Use the delegated refresh path when enabled and initialize the connection with its returned tokens.

findings.title: Handle minimal sync responses separately from native provider responses
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens documents that the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but the delegated Webex response still goes through webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A valid minimal sync response is therefore rejected at the first refresh. Lark's delegated path similarly still expects its native code/data envelope and refresh-token fields. Add sync-specific parsing and preserve existing credential metadata rather than requiring the parent to return the native refresh-token response.

findings.title: Identify the connected account before replacing its credentials
findings.body: A user can have multiple credentials for the same app, including multiple Google Calendar accounts, but the webhook identifies a connection only by userId and appSlug and overwrites findFirst's result. A sync intended for the second account can replace the first account's tokens while leaving calendar selections and booking references attached to that first credential ID. Accept a stable connection/account identifier, or reject ambiguous matches rather than silently choosing one.

findings.title: Make initial credential synchronization idempotent under concurrency
findings.body: The existence lookup and credential creation are separate operations. Two overlapping deliveries for a previously unsynced connection can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Subsequent deliveries update only one row through findFirst, leaving the duplicate with stale tokens. Use an atomic or serialized operation keyed by the synced connection so concurrent webhook deliveries cannot create duplicates.

findings.title: Clear credential invalidation when fresh credentials are synced
findings.body: Google, Zoom, and Webex can mark a credential invalid after an unrecoverable grant error. If the user reconnects in the parent application, this webhook finds that existing row but updates only its key, leaving invalid=true despite the replacement tokens. The credential remains marked disconnected and unavailable to consumers that exclude invalid credentials. Reset the invalid flag when accepting validated replacement credentials.
